ledger.x: 10 April 1941: the NDH is a German client from its birth.
18 May 1941: the Treaties of Rome give Italy the Dalmatian coast and islands.
10 September 1943: the NDH takes back the ceded coast.
8 September 1943: Italy capitulates and the protectorate ends ('a protectorate of Fascist Italy from 1941 to 1943'; 'On 8 September 1943, Italy capitulated').
Late 1944: the Partisans hold most of the Dalmatian coast.
March 1945: the Partisan side of the Syrmian contest passes to the new state.
March 1945: the Syrmian Front continues against the Yugoslavia of the 8 March coalition government.

wars.name: Invasion of Yugoslavia
wars.outcome: Yugoslavia partitioned: the NDH proclaimed on 10 April 1941, the war ended 'with the unconditional surrender signed by General Danilo Kalafatović on 17 April'; Hungary took Vojvodina, Baranja, Bačka and Međimurje and Italy took Dalmatian land.

wars.name: World War II in Yugoslavia
wars.outcome: The Partisans take the interior, the Dalmatian coast and Bosnia in 1944-1945 and the NDH government dissolves on 8 May 1945.

certainty.note: A puppet state split into German and Italian zones by an undated line of demarcation, with the interior held by the Partisans from 1942; only the Dalmatian line of the Treaties of Rome of 18 May 1941 and the Hungarian annexation line are…
